title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_0RE1LD_0LB1LD_---1RC_1RA0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_0RE1LD_0LB1LD_---1RC_1RA0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Its tape is two counters side by side: at the start of every pass it reads 0 0 (10)^a 1^b 10. A pass doubles a, paid for out of b; when b runs short the head bounces off the right end and continues, like a ball folding a strip. The pass-to-pass map on (a, b) is a Collatz-like piecewise linear map with slope 2. Lean proves the whole map, rebounds included, and proves that the machine halts if and only if the map reaches a pass start with at most one 1 in the right block.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to the map. Lean proves, for all parameters, every case of the phase map (plain rounds, the end of a pass, the rebounds off the right end and the special small cases), and proves that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if iterating that map from the first pass start reaches B>0 0 (10)^a 1^c with c ≤ 1 (halts_iff). By native_decide the first 108 phases (about 2·107 passes) do not; a Python copy of the map runs 108 passes without it.

Where a halt would come from. From B>0 0 (10)^n followed by blank tape the machine halts within a few steps (C and E zip right over the 10s and E reads a blank). That is the tape after a pass that ends with b = 0, which needs a coincidence of size about 1/width, and only in rare stretches where b is even.

Why it has not halted. b is odd for long stretches (an odd b can never become 0), and the even stretches are short chains of doublings, each with a chance of order 1/width to hit 0. Iterating the map for 108 passes (tape width 2·108) gives no halt; the closest pass ended with b = 2. A proof would have to control this arithmetic coincidence, as for a Collatz-type problem.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 2,938 cells have been visited and 1,548 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The phase map, all cases
claims.text: Write PS a c for 0^inf B>0 0 (10)^a 1^c 0^inf (a pass start) and Q R m c for 0^inf (10)^R (11)^m A> 1^c 0^inf (inside a pass). For all parameters the machine goes: PS (a+1) (c+2) → Q a 2 (c+2); PS 0 2 → PS 0 5; PS 0 (c+3) → PS 2 (c+1); j rounds Q (R+j) (m+2) (c+2j+1) → Q R (m+2+2j) (c+1); end Q 0 (m+2) (c+5) → PS (m+4) (c+1); the special ends Q 0 (m+2) c for c = 1, 2, 3, 4 → PS 0 (2m+8), PS 0 (2m+6), PS 0 (2m+11), PS 0 (2m+9); the rebounds Q 1 (m+2) c → PS 2 (2m+6), PS 2 (2m+4) and Q (R+2) (m+2) c → Q R 2 (2m+8), Q R 2 (2m+6) for c = 1, 2. Each case is one symbolic run (or an induction over rounds); next is this map.
claims.where: next, next_sound, q_rounds, lean/Phases.lean; the runs in lean/Pieces.lean (generated by lean/pieces.py); tape normalisation tape_eq, lean/Norm.lean

claims.title: Halting is equivalent to the map reaching c ≤ 1
claims.text: The run from blank tape reaches PS 0 2 after 4 steps; PS a 0 and PS a 1 halt; on every configuration the map reaches, next is defined except there. Hence the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from PS 0 2 is PS a c with c ≤ 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> phases
claims.text: Iterating next from PS 0 2, the first 108 phases (20,000,581 pass starts) contain no PS a c with c ≤ 1, by compiled evaluation. So a halt, if any, comes after more than 2·107 passes, far beyond the 3,100 passes direct simulation reaches in 1010 steps.

claims.title: The plain pass
claims.text: For all a, s and every tape R after the block of 1s: from B>0 0 (10)^(a+2) 1^(s+2a+7) R, blank to the left, the machine reaches B>0 0 (10)^(2a+6) 1^(s+1) R. In pass-map terms (a, b) → (2a + 2, b − 2a − 2) whenever a ≥ 2 and b ≥ 2a + 3. (The first version of the proof; the phase map above contains it.)

claims.title: The pass map agrees with the runs and with Lean's map
claims.text: pass_map (written in terms of (a, b, t), b + t being the c of PS a c) reproduces every one of the 3,095 passes in the first 1010 steps of the C simulator, and lean_next, a case-by-case copy of Lean's next, agrees with it at every one of 108 pass starts.

claims.title: 10<sup>8</sup> passes of the map, no halt
claims.text: Iterated from the first pass start, the map runs 108 passes (tape width 2·108) without reaching c ≤ 1. Only 166 passes end with b even; b ≤ 5 happened 35 times, b = 2 once. With halts_iff this is a statement about the machine, resting on the Python code (exact integer arithmetic) instead of Lean.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.348). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting is equivalent (proved in Lean) to the phase map reaching a pass start with c ≤ 1, an arithmetic coincidence that the map avoids for 10<sup>8</sup> passes and that gets rarer as the tape grows, but nothing rules it out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a Collatz-like map on two counters, and it would halt only if one pass of that map ended exactly at zero. This page runs the real machine in your browser, explains the map, and lists what is known.

facts.text: The whole phase map, rebounds included, proved for all parameters.
The first 10<sup>8</sup> phases of the proved map: no halt.
No halt in the C simulator; 3,095 passes, all as the pass map says.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The tape at every pass start: two counters.
The map, iterated: no pass ends with b = 0, the one way to halt.

sections.heading: Two counters on one tape
html: Run the simulator for a while and stop when the head is at the left end in state B. The tape always has the same simple form: two blank cells, then a copies of 10, then a solid block of b ones, then (usually) one more 10:

So the machine is a device with two counters. A few of the pass starts from the first 4,000 steps, as (a, b): (2, 35), (6, 29), (14, 15), (12, 21), (2, 43), (6, 37), (14, 23). The total width 2a + b grows by 2 with each pass, so the tape grows only as fast as the number of passes, and each pass takes time proportional to about the square of the width: after 109 steps the tape is about 2,900 cells wide.

sections.heading: One pass: doubling, folded
html: In a pass, state A walks back and forth eating the 10s on the left one at a time. Each eaten 10 costs two 1s from the right block and adds four 1s to a block that grows in the middle. When the 10s are used up, the middle block becomes the new run of 10s. If b is large enough this is simply

as in (2, 35) → (6, 29) → (14, 15). When the right block runs out first, the head rebounds off the right end: the middle block becomes the new right block (about twice as long as the old one) and eating continues. So a pass is a little Euclid-like loop, and (14, 15) goes to (12, 21): seven 10s eaten, a rebound, then the last six. With a few more rules for the rare even cases this pass_map (in py/passmap.py) predicts every one of the 3,095 passes in the first 1010 steps exactly. Every case, rebounds included, is proved in Lean for all parameters (next_sound in lean/Phases.lean).

Measured against the width, a is being doubled and folded back, like the tent map x → 2x on a strip. That is why the tape contents look irregular: the sequence of a's is as erratic as the binary digits of a number.

sections.heading: Halting needs b = 0
html: The only halting transition is E reading a 0. E is entered only from C reading a 0, and C and E together zip rightwards over 0 1 0 1 …, C on the 0s and E on the 1s. That zipper starts only at a pass start, on the two blank cells, and it runs over all the 10s. If a solid block follows, C reads a 1 and turns back. If the 10s are followed by blank tape, E reads a blank and the machine halts: from B>0 0 (10)^n it stops after 2n + 5 steps (proved in Lean for every n, zip_halts).

So the machine halts exactly when a pass ends with b = 0 and the closing 10 present. The width 2a + b + 2 has the parity of b, and the map changes that parity only at rare special passes; for long stretches b is odd and can never reach 0. In the short stretches where b is even, a goes through a chain of plain doublings and the next value of b is 0 only if 2a + 2 equals b exactly, a coincidence of probability about 1/width.

Iterating the map (much faster than the machine) for 108 passes, out to a tape 2·108 cells wide: only 166 passes end with an even b, the smallest b was 2, and no pass ends at 0. The expected number of future hits, summing 1/width over the even passes, is tiny and shrinking, so the machine very probably never halts; but proving it means controlling where the doubling map lands, a Collatz-type question. Lean proves that this is exactly the question: the machine halts if and only if the map reaches a pass start with at most one 1 in the right block (halts_iff).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.348). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 2,938 cells (2,350 left of the start, 23 right), with a density of 1s of 0.527.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Collatz-like pass map on two counters
summary: Two counters a and b, tape 0 0 (10)^a 1^b 10; each pass doubles a against b with Euclid-like rebounds, and it halts only if a pass ends with b = 0, which the map has avoided for 10^8 passes.
